english: Let $d$ denote the minimum distance between the curves $y=x^{2}$ and $y=-\left(x-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}$. Then the value of $d^{2}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $d$ वक्रों $y=x^{2}$ तथा $y=-\left(x-\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^{2}$ के बीच की न्यूनतम दूरी को दर्शाता है। तब $d^{2}$ का मान ______ है।
solution: The curves do not meet ($x^{2}\ge0\ge -\left(x-\frac32\right)^{2}$, never both zero). At the nearest pair the tangents are parallel and the joining segment is a common normal.
Slopes $2a$ at $(a,a^{2})$ and $-2\left(b-\frac32\right)$ at $Q$ equal $\Rightarrow b=\frac32-a$, $Q\left(\frac32-a,-a^{2}\right)$.
$P\left(\frac12,\frac14\right)$, $Q\left(1,-\frac14\right)$; the parallel tangents $y=x-\frac14$ and $y=x-\frac54$ separate the convex curves, so this is the minimum.
solution_full: The first curve lies on or above the $x$-axis and the second on or below it, and they cannot both be $0$ at the same $x$, so the curves are disjoint and the minimum distance is positive.

Let $P(a,a^{2})$ and $Q\left(b,-\left(b-\frac32\right)^{2}\right)$ be the nearest points. Then $PQ$ is normal to both curves, so the tangent slopes are equal: $2a=-2\left(b-\frac32\right)$, i.e. $b=\frac32-a$ and $Q=\left(\frac32-a,-a^{2}\right)$.

$\overrightarrow{PQ}=\left(\frac32-2a,-2a^{2}\right)$ must be parallel to the normal direction $(-2a,1)$ of $y=x^{2}$ at $P$: $\left(\frac32-2a\right)\cdot1-(-2a^{2})(-2a)=0$, i.e. $4a^{3}+2a-\frac32=0$, or $8a^{3}+4a-3=0$.

Why this is the minimum: the tangent to $y=x^{2}$ at $P$ is $y=x-\frac14$ and the tangent to the second curve at $Q$ is $y=x-\frac54$. The convex curve $y=x^{2}$ lies above its tangent and the concave curve lies below its tangent, so every segment joining the curves crosses the strip between these parallel lines, whose width is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$. Hence the distance is at least $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$, and $PQ=\dfrac{1}{\sqrt2}$ attains it.
originality_note: New: two opposite parabolas that are point-symmetric about (3/4, 0); the common normal is found through equal slopes and the minimum is justified by two parallel separating tangents (way 4). Closest known: minimum distance between y^2 = 4x and x^2 = -32y type pairs, or curve-to-line distance. Different because: the pair is neither a curve and a line nor an inverse pair, and the minimality argument uses the separating strip.

concept_use.Minimum distance between two curves: Common-normal condition with equal slopes gives P(1/2,1/4), Q(1,-1/4) and d^2 = 1/2.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (decimal between 0 and 1); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Checked the curves are disjoint so the minimum is positive and attained. No change.
key_step: Equal slopes at the nearest points give b = 3/2 - a; the normal condition reduces to 8a^3 + 4a - 3 = 0.
justification: Routine common-normal computation ending in a cubic with an obvious root; no insight beyond the standard method, L2 like the conic-tangent anchor 2026-P2-Q17.
